contents.text:
Hello,

Your M3 - Reply Detector caught a new client reply, but it was forced to pause because Make.com lost its connection to your Notion workspace.

⚠️ UNPROCESSED CLIENT REPLY

Because the system couldn't access Notion, the following email was NOT logged, and the client's status was not updated:

  • From: {{1.fromEmail}}
  • Subject: {{1.subject}}

🔍 WHY DID THIS HAPPEN?

This usually occurs due to routine security expirations. Your Notion authorization in Make.com has likely expired, or the "Clients" database was accidentally moved or deleted.

🛠️ HOW TO FIX IT IN 2 MINUTES

  • Step 1: Reauthorize Notion. Go to your Make.com dashboard, open your M3 scenario, click on the Notion module, and hit the "Reauthorize" (or Refresh) button to renew the connection.
  • Step 2: Manual Update. Go to your Gmail inbox, read the email from the client listed above, and manually update their status in Notion.

Once you reauthorize Notion, the automation will naturally resume working for all future emails.

Best regards,
Revenue Recovery Engine

You are an "Intent Classifier" assistant. Read the incoming customer email text and classify their intent into one of these 4 categories:

"positive" (positive reply, wants a meeting, asking questions, requesting info, interested),

"objection" (finds it expensive, bad timing, has a specific objection),

"ooo" (out of office auto-reply, on vacation),

"unsubscribe" (remove me from the list, not interested, stop emailing),

"unknown" (cannot classify the intent, complex or unrelated message).

Output ONLY in JSON format exactly like this: {"classification": "selected_category"}

mapper.subject: ⚠️ URGENT: Notion Schema Error in Reply Detector

contents.text:
Hello,

Your M3 - Reply Detector successfully received and analyzed a client's email, but it encountered a critical error while trying to save the data back to your Notion workspace.

👤 CLIENT DETAILS

  • Name: {{4.properties_value.Name[].plain_text}}
  • Email: {{1.fromEmail}}
  • Subject: {{1.subject}}
  • AI Detected Intent: {{7.result.classification}}

🚨 WHY DID THIS HAPPEN?

This error happens when Make.com cannot find the exact database columns it needs to update. It means a required property in your "Clients" database has been renamed, deleted, or its property type was accidentally changed (e.g., changing a "Select" property to a "Text" property).

In this specific step, the system was trying to update the following columns. One of these is likely missing or altered:

  • Status
  • Reply Status
  • Reply Received
  • Replied At
  • Last Inbound Message ID

🛠️ HOW TO FIX IT IN 2 MINUTES

  • Step 1: Check your Notion Database. Open your "Clients" database and verify that all the columns listed above exist exactly as they were in the original template. Ensure their property types (Select, Checkbox, Date, Text) haven't been changed.
  • Step 2: Save this Lead. Go to your Gmail, read the email from {{1.fromEmail}}, and manually update their status in Notion. (This is critical: Since the system failed to save, this client might still be marked as "Active" and could receive unwanted automated follow-ups.)

Once you fix the column names in Notion, the automation will naturally resume working for future emails.

Best regards,
Revenue Recovery Engine

Hello,

Your M3 - Reply Detector caught an email, but processing was aborted because of a configuration error in your Notion workspace.

🚨 MULTIPLE CONFIGURATION ROWS DETECTED

The system found more than one row in your "System Settings" database. Make.com requires exactly ONE active row to properly load your AI prompts and operational rules.

🛠️ HOW TO FIX IT

  • Step 1: Clean up Notion. Open your "System Settings" database. Find and delete the extra/empty rows. Keep only your main configuration row.
  • Step 2: Check the latest email. Since the system halted, the email from {{1.fromEmail}} was NOT processed. Please check it manually in your inbox.

Best regards,
Revenue Recovery Engine
